title: Redstrike Surface-Coverage Ledger
description: Per-engagement record of which DISCOVERED attack-surface elements (endpoints, params, identities, forms, API operations, sinks, headers, uploads, auth flows — plus, for a white-box audit, entry-points / source-leads / high-risk-files) were actually CONSUMED by an executor vs merely discovered by recon. Category coverage (coverage_ledger.json) proves which vuln CLASSES ran; this proves how much of the real SURFACE each class was tested against. A surface discovered but never tested (and not skipped with a reason) is a recall gap a category-level ledger cannot see. Produced by scripts/surface.py --plan from the recon feeders (and, when source access is granted, from app_model.json + source_context.json), updated with --mark as executors consume each element.

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the plan/last update.

kind.description: what kind of surface element this is. The last five are the white-box / source-audit surface the code-audit executor consumes: entry-point, source_context.json lead, high-risk file, plus two FIRST-CLASS enumerated surfaces grep/taint cannot assert — state-op (a state-changing operation + the invariant it must hold, for the business-logic/concurrency TOCTOU pass) and authz-route (a route x its required-privilege cell, for the authorization-matrix pass).

value.description: the element itself (path, param name, identity label, sink location, entry-point symbol@file:line, source-lead id, high-risk file path...).

routed_to.description: category ids whose executors SHOULD consume this element.

status.description: discovered=enumerated, NOT yet fed to any executor (a gap if still so at close); tested=an executor consumed it; skipped=deliberately not tested (needs reason); n/a=routes to no in-scope category.

consumed_by.description: executor/skill ids that tested this element.
